newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Menem bucks call to boycott "Evita".
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem bucks call to boycott "Evita".

text.p: Spurning the advice of his closest aide, Argentine President Carlos Menem said on Wednesday he would see the controversial movie "Evita."
The musical opened on last Thursday in Buenos Aires to protests and pesticide attacks after Vice-President Carlos Ruckauf called for a boycott.
Ruckauf said Alan Parker's film was "an insult" to the memory of Argentina's legendary first lady Eva Peron. But he admitted having seen only video clips of the film, which stars pop idol Madonna.
"That's the opinion of a colleague I respect, but I don't think in the same way," Menem said of the boycott. "First I want to see the movie and then I will give my opinion."

Three theatres had to be evacuated briefly when pesticide spray devices were set off as the musical opened on Thursday. Critics also loudly protested its portrayal of Evita as a woman who manipulates men through sex to gain political power.

Evita, the wife of populist leader Juan Domingo Peron, championed the cause of the working class and died of cancer in 1952 when she was just 33. She is still revered by many Argentines as a saint for her charity work and defence of workers, whom she affectionately called "my shirtless ones."
Menem said he had watched 15 minutes of the film which Parker sent him two months ago. "The bit I saw was excellent, but I can't speak about the rest yet," he said.
The Peronist Party leader also blasted critics who say he should not have allowed Parker to film from a balcony of the presidential palace overlooking historic Plaza de Mayo.
Juan and Eva Peron made their most famous speeches from the balcony, where Madonna sang "Don't Cry for Me Argentina".

"Who were the ones who spun all those rumours about the life of Evita -- Argentines or outsiders?", asked Menem, the political heir of the general who was ousted by a coup in 1955 and returned to power briefly in 1973.

"Many say they are outraged, but they forget that the real victim of the military coup of 1955 was Eva Peron, whose dead body was mutilated and raped by Argentines, not outsiders," said Menem, referring to attacks on Eva's embalmed body.
"Evita" is a film adaptation of the original Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber stage musical, which for many years was banned in Argentina.
